scenarios.title: Long-list disclosure anchor with measured scroll-boundary headroom
steps: Run Prepare long-list disclosure diagnosis in a fresh disposable Vault. This creates Disclosure with 120 siblings and 498 children under Node 060/Wide, and starts the frame recorder. Do not use the initial short fixture as this scenario's evidence.

Expand Disclosure and scroll Node 060 to the middle of the viewport, with more than one viewport of scroll headroom in both directions. Expand Node 060, then expand/collapse Wide repeatedly and collapse/re-expand Node 060 while Wide is expanded. Keep the pointer at the disclosure control and do not scroll during a sample.

Repeat with the active note in a different branch, and separately near the bottom scroll boundary. Save Explorer navigation frames. Inspect the pre-click sample and subsequent samples through at least 750 ms. Keep boundary samples separate from eligible middle-viewport samples.
Compare the same middle-viewport disclosure with Folder Nodes disabled and enabled. Restore the candidate to enabled before finishing. Record the actual theme and viewport.
expected: Every claimed middle-viewport observation has a clicked-row target, complete nonempty frames, and middleViewportEligible=true. Missing rows, empty frames or insufficient boundary headroom are unverified, never a pass.

Away from scroll limits, the clicked row stays within one CSS pixel of its pre-click vertical position throughout expansion and collapse, including the final position. Record topRange and finalDelta; do not infer animation smoothness from endpoint screenshots alone.
Boundary clamping and native-host behavior are reported separately. Preparation, frame collection and native comparison do not assign a product pass by themselves.

With Folder Nodes enabled, bottom-boundary disclosure also keeps the clicked row within one CSS pixel by retaining necessary space. Scroll upward to reclaim space; repeated downward scrolling must not grow blank space. Record the disabled native baseline separately.

scenarios.title: Deep breadcrumb reveal, native ordering handoff and visible viewport anchoring
steps: Run the acceptance provider Create deep Explorer reveal fixture command. Open Reveal/Node 060/Level Two/Level Three/Leaf/Leaf.md, collapse its Explorer ancestors and scroll away.

Activate each note breadcrumb ancestor repeatedly with Reveal in Manual mode. Check the first visible frame, about 100 ms and about 500 ms after navigation; on desktop also test a collapsed sidebar and a pop-out window.
Reveal a different branch through a Folder Nodes menu while the active note remains elsewhere. Scroll away from the active note and expand an unrelated branch, including near the scroll limits.

Switch Reveal to Name, change the native Explorer sort, switch to Manual, then change native sort again. Create, rename and remove disposable child nodes through the product before switching back to Name.
Compare breadcrumb navigation with Folder Nodes disabled and enabled in this disposable Vault. Restore the candidate to enabled before finishing.
expected: The target remains visible after navigation settles, with no second ordering jump or wrong ancestor expansion. Desktop pop-out navigation uses the relevant window.
Ordinary refresh preserves the visible rows and never pulls the viewport toward an offscreen active note. Explicit reveal exposes the requested branch.
Name follows the current host sibling sort, including newly created and renamed nodes; Manual applies child ranks without touching unrelated entries.
The disabled comparison distinguishes host behavior from candidate behavior and does not substitute for enabled-candidate observations.

scenarios.title: Hidden node and inherited descendant projection
steps: Confirm the explicit hidden root and its descendant are absent from Folder Nodes projections
Use the eye beside Root to enable session reveal and inspect the explicit Hidden text badge and inherited source treatment
Disable Apply hidden markers and reload without editing frontmatter
While the subtree is hidden, use a Node action to Reveal in File Explorer and click the active note breadcrumb for that hidden path; then enable the Root eye and repeat.
expected: Only Folder Nodes Explorer, Contents, and Graph projections hide the marked subtree
The explicit root has one non-interactive Hidden text badge, no per-node eye, and the descendant shows inherited muted feedback
Session reveal resets on reload and the hidden=true token remains byte-preserved

Folder Nodes never reports its own reveal as successful while the target path is property-hidden. Native breadcrumb expansion does not override the plugin projection; after session reveal is enabled, both paths can expose the target without editing frontmatter.

scenarios.title: Preview-first structure and property migration, selection creation, and sparse ordering
steps: Preview leaf-note and missing-node organization before committing it
Preview legacy Folder Nodes properties, confirm the conflict blocks writes, resolve it, then explicitly migrate
Create a child node from the selected fixture text after confirming creation location, short node name, and alias policy
Exercise before, into, and after placement using the available platform interaction
expected: No Vault write occurs before either explicit preview confirmation
Legacy tokens migrate to one folder-nodes list while unrelated YAML stays unchanged
The modal omits the full Node Note path and raw wikilink while selection replacement still uses the correct Vault-relative wikilink
Manual order uses only order=manual on the parent and child-owned sparse rank tokens

scenarios.title: Leaf affordance, compact Contents header, and stable graph focus
steps: Inspect a complete visual leaf in File Explorer, then add a visible direct file
Open Node Contents for a deep node, toggle one non-empty section, and navigate away and back

Focus a deep graph node and collapse its parent directly and with Collapse to level 1; on desktop also use Alt to collapse the whole branch, and on Android use the equivalent branch action from the node menu.
Select a parent, view its subtree, then select a child without changing scope; explicitly view the child subtree and return to global
Use the icon, expansion handle, context menu and File Explorer reveal; on desktop also exercise keyboard navigation. Inspect matching handle backgrounds and stable expansion anchors.
expected: The hidden canonical note yields a passive dot, and visible content restores the native disclosure arrow
Breadcrumbs contain ancestors only, the current node appears once, empty sections are absent, and section disclosure survives the view session
Direct and whole-branch operations select their card; range collapse moves hidden focus to the nearest visible ancestor in DOM or Canvas rendering
The scope status names its root independently from the selected card; actions name the selected target and disable only for the same root and mode
Selection and expansion agree across renderers; position, scale and toggle keyboard focus survive redraws; File Explorer reveals the targeted folder

scenarios.title: Short context menus and grouped Folder Nodes actions
steps: Open a complete Folder Node menu from Contents, Graph, File Explorer, and its Node Note tab
Open Folder Nodes actions and inspect Open, Appearance, Structure, and Management groups
Inspect first/last sibling, inherited-hidden, native folder, and Node Note surfaces
expected: The first level stays short and native file or folder actions remain present
Boundary reorder actions are disabled and subtree-wide actions use explicit wording
The grouped action panel is keyboard accessible and touch targets are at least 44px

scenarios.title: Current-node icon containment and small-graph viewport anchors
steps: Inspect Node Contents for Geometry and its Emoji, Glyph, Image, and Lucide children in a narrow pane.
Open the Geometry subtree in DOM 2D, expand and collapse branches with the graph smaller than the viewport and then larger than it, and scroll to the upper and left edges.
Repeat appearance checks with Default and Minimal themes in light and dark modes.
expected: Each current-node visual stays inside its left handle without overlapping or clipping the title.
Expansion and collapse preserve the selected node screen position and all graph content remains reachable by scrolling.
Handles and titles remain legible in all four theme and mode combinations.

scenarios.title: Explicit ordering, unmanaged visibility, and stable refresh
steps: Open Placement and verify _Unmanaged/_Unmanaged.md remains visible in the native Explorer.
Move Placement/Move into Placement/Natural using desktop drag or the Move action. Confirm natural ordering is unchanged.
Open Placement/Manual and use Child order to switch between Name and Manual; use the platform reorder action to change a child position.

On desktop compare the equivalent A-after and B-before gaps with hidden nodes revealed, and verify hidden-gap feedback while they are hidden. On Android verify disabled reorder actions in Name mode and enabled actions in Manual mode.
Open Contents and keep a section disclosure focused while its node icon metadata changes; verify focus retention, then edit only a note body and check that the node list stays stable.
expected: Unmanaged same-named Markdown remains visible; ordinary reparenting does not enable manual ordering.
Sorting is explicitly controlled on the parent and the resulting child order persists.
Desktop gaps match their visible destination and reject hidden ambiguities; Android uses the same explicit ordering rules through menus.
Contents remains usable after refresh and unrelated body edits do not reset its node list.

scenarios.title: Passive Explorer disclosures and active-note creation destination
steps: In File Explorer tap or click the passive dot of a complete leaf with no visible contents; then activate its title separately.
Expand and collapse Geometry repeatedly while an unrelated branch is visible. Add a direct file to the leaf and repeat disclosure activation.
Reload with no Explorer folder selected, open Geometry/Emoji/Emoji.md, then switch to Geometry/Glyph/Glyph.md through an already-open note tab and use the Explorer New node button.
Set File Explorer to a native non-name sort, reveal a folder through the active note breadcrumb, then switch the containing parent between Name and Manual child order.
expected: The passive dot neither opens a note nor expands the row. The title opens its Node Note once.
Normal disclosures remain native, visible contents restore the arrow, and unrelated rows and scroll position remain stable.
The creation dialog names Geometry/Glyph as the destination after the active-note switch; cancel the dialog after verifying its destination.

Name mode leaves native File Explorer sibling order untouched; Manual mode applies Folder Nodes ranks without a second visible jump and the revealed active branch remains at the same viewport position.

scenarios.title: Viewport toolbar, scope and focus remain independent
steps: Open the Geometry subtree in DOM 2D. Select an off-center node and use zoom in, zoom out, percentage reset and Fit.
Switch to 3D and repeat the toolbar operations; inspect the interaction help in a narrow pane.
On Android scroll DOM 2D with one finger and verify that the zoom, percentage and help controls have touch targets at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels.
expected: The percentage updates immediately and reset returns to 100%; zoom preserves the viewport-center anchor.
Fit contains the graph where permitted by readable node sizes without changing the subtree scope or selection.
Toolbar actions do not open a node or change selection, and the toolbar remains usable in a narrow mobile pane.

scenarios.title: Desktop anchors across DOM and Canvas boundaries
steps: In a fresh disposable Vault, run the acceptance provider command Create 501-node viewport fixture, scope the graph to Viewport, and retain the default large-graph threshold of 500.

In DOM 2D, test ordinary wheel scrolling, Ctrl/Cmd+wheel zoom at an off-center card near the upper-left scroll boundary, and blank-space mouse dragging. Test + and - for zoom and 0 for Fit with graph focus, then confirm they do not hijack the search input.
Select Wide and expand it to cross from 3 visible nodes to 501; pan, zoom above 400% and below 65%, then collapse it to return to DOM. Repeat near both zoom limits and all viewport edges.
Repeat expansion, collapse, off-center pointer zoom, percentage reset and Fit in 3D with both renderers.
expected: Unmodified wheel scrolls while Ctrl/Cmd+wheel zooms around its pointer; blank dragging pans without opening nodes.
Selection, scope, supported zoom and the expansion-card screen anchor survive both renderer transitions without a visible jump.
Zoom limits do not move the anchored point, all graph content remains reachable, and search typing retains normal text behavior.
3D pointer zoom preserves its projected anchor and both renderers expose the same toolbar actions.

scenarios.title: Android native pinch and two-finger pan across graph renderers
steps: Confirm the input host receives two simultaneous native touch pointers with distinct identities and releases both after cancellation or completion.

Generate the 501-node Viewport fixture in a fresh disposable Vault and expand Wide to enter Canvas 2D. Pinch at an off-center midpoint, translate both fingers together, then combine scaling and translation.
Repeat in DOM 3D with Wide collapsed and Canvas 3D with Wide expanded. Exercise zoom limits, toolbar reset, Fit and expansion across the 500-node renderer boundary.
After each two-finger gesture, lift both fingers and tap or long-press a card normally. In DOM 2D use native one-finger scrolling and toolbar zoom.
expected: Pinch preserves the world point under its moving midpoint and same-distance two-finger movement pans without rotating the 3D camera.
Two-finger gestures do not accidentally select, open or invoke a context menu for a node.
Supported zoom and selected-card position remain stable across renderer changes; percentage and controls stay synchronized.
No pointer remains captured after release or cancellation, and ordinary interaction resumes.

scenarios.title: Complete interface languages, persisted selection and scoped Arabic RTL
steps: In a fresh disposable Vault, open Folder Nodes settings and switch through English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Vietnamese and Arabic. Inspect all five tabs and return to General for each language. Follow Obsidian must resolve to the actual host language when supported, or English otherwise.

In German and Russian, inspect long setting descriptions, menus, command names and the Node Graph toolbar at narrow width. Keep a graph open while switching languages; its tab, navigation header and active-window title must update while the search and viewport remain. On desktop, inspect host-aligned cursors on settings tabs and graph drag surfaces. Inspect Arabic settings right-to-left layout, visible focus, numbers, icons, and the mixed Latin/Arabic Localization node path. On desktop exercise direction-aware Left/Right plus Home/End tab navigation; on Android use touch and horizontal tab scrolling.

While Arabic is selected, change the Canvas node/edge threshold to 600 using the real input control, leave and reopen settings, and confirm it is retained. Open a path-rule dialog for the mixed Latin/Arabic fixture and cancel without applying a rule. Verify that ordinary Obsidian UI outside the plugin settings is not redirected by the plugin.

Inspect translated command-palette entries, a node menu and the mobile ribbon menu after changing language. The existing ribbon action must retain its identity and position while its label updates. Disable and re-enable Folder Nodes through the host UI, then reopen its settings and confirm the selected language and threshold remain. Switch back to Follow Obsidian and check the resolved language. Do not create, rename, move, delete or migrate fixture notes in this scenario.
expected: All twelve selections render their translated tabs and settings without missing keys or unexpected English fallback. Long descriptions and critical controls remain readable; narrow tabs remain reachable. Automatic selection follows the supported host locale.

Arabic reverses only the plugin-owned settings surface. Mixed-script paths, icons and numbers remain usable; desktop keyboard focus follows the visible tab direction. Command and node-menu text updates to the selected language.

The selected language and numeric threshold survive closing settings and a real plugin disable/enable cycle. The host outside plugin settings retains its own direction. Fixture note bytes, names and structural properties remain unchanged.

scenarios.title: Relative and removed-note link refusal with final merge lifecycle/editor revalidation
steps: Use a fresh disposable Vault with the fixture app.json: automatic internal-link updates are disabled. Confirm that host option before running Prepare merge safety fixture. Save and close all source, target and descendant editors before each merge. Use the product Merge node action on each case's Source, selecting its Deep/Target.

Try Inline, Definition and Nested. Definition uses a destination on the line after [ref]:. Confirm a refusal notice and inspect the original notes, target body, child paths and attachments. The original and destination directories contain different Reference.md files.

In a fresh Inline source case, replace its body with a WikiLink resolving to its own Source Node Note. Try basename and full Vault path, display alias, heading, block reference and embed forms in separate reset cases; also place one such reference in a moved child note. Save and close editors before using Merge node. Inspect unchanged source/target bytes and child paths after each refusal.

Repeat the removed-note reference as a Text property and a List property in the source note, then in a moved child note. Confirm refusal before mutations; an unrelated property link still transfers normally. Include a list-scoped code fence followed by a real link in the next list item to confirm that the real link is checked.

Repeat the removed-note link case with the text present only inside fenced code, inline code or comments, with a valid unrelated WikiLink outside those literals. Confirm the literals do not themselves block an otherwise safe merge. Reset before the next case.

Merge Safe using the product UI. Open the appended attachment link and moved child, then inspect the surviving attachment and target note. Confirm only this successful source folder is removed according to the host deletion setting.

Run Arm merge editor race, then merge EditorRace/Source through the product UI. The provider opens the source editor at the final descendant read. Inspect the refusal, source editor content, restored child path and target body. Close that editor before continuing.

Run Arm merge unload race, then merge UnloadRace/Source through the product UI. The provider disables the candidate at the final descendant read. Inspect source/child preservation and target rollback; re-enable Folder Nodes through the host UI. Run Save merge safety observations and record the real host environment.
expected: Unsafe inline and multiline reference links in source or descendant notes refuse before any move, append or source removal. WikiLinks and embeds that resolve to the removed source Node Note also refuse before mutations, including aliases and heading/block fragments; code and comments remain literal.
A supported relative attachment moving with the source retains its target after a successful merge.

Both deterministic final-read races actually trigger in the live host. Unload and a reopened source editor prevent source removal, preserve user content and compensate already dispatched owned changes.
Provider output records observations only; actual product actions and host state determine the scoped verdict.

scenarios.title: Bound icon and cover editing across concurrent changes and unload
steps: In a fresh disposable Vault, open the Visual Picker for Geometry/Lucide. Change icon from another editor or host window while the picker remains open, then confirm the old picker. Verify the newer icon and note body remain. Reset the fixture and repeat after renaming or replacing the original Node Note or folder.

Open a fresh picker and disable Folder Nodes through the host UI while it is open. Confirm the picker closes and cannot submit after re-enable. Open a new picker, save a valid list, then remove its icon normally to verify successful writes still work.

On desktop use Tab and the move/remove buttons to reorder and delete visual candidates. Confirm keyboard focus remains on the moved candidate or an adjacent surviving row. On Android exercise the equivalent touch controls and verify the intended list order.

Open Set as visual for a Vault image, then replace or rename that image or the target Node Note before activating the retained menu where the host allows it. Verify stale actions leave the note unchanged. Use a freshly opened menu to set a valid cover and inspect the resolved image. If the host closes the menu before the concurrent change can be reproduced, record that boundary as unverified rather than claiming a pass.
expected: Edits retain the original folder, canonical note, paths and icon value. Concurrent replacement, rename or icon changes refuse stale edits without changing newer content.
Plugin unload invalidates old pickers and prevents new writes from their callbacks. A new picker after re-enable can save and delete icons normally.
Keyboard or touch list operations remain usable, and unchanged cover actions resolve the selected Vault image.
Record desktop and Android observations separately. Adapter callback-delay tests do not prove that a particular host interleaving was observed.

scenarios.title: Quoted-key protection, recognized note renaming and stable settings rules
steps: Try hiding SafetyQuoted, whose canonical node property uses an escaped quoted key; verify the operation refuses and original note bytes are unchanged.
Hide and show SafetyPlain; verify the unknown future token and its comment survive.
Rename SafetyRename through the product prompt; verify its recognized safetyrename.MD note follows the folder and retains its content. Cancel a prompt before confirming the intended rename.
Remove two explicitly added temporary unmanaged rules through settings and verify the intended rows disappear. Inspect localized help at narrow width.
expected: Ambiguous quoted source keys fail before writes.
Supported property edits preserve unknown tokens and comments.
The actual recognized note is renamed, and cancelling does not mutate it.
Rule removal and localized settings remain usable.
